harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured sudo on node1 to log every sudo-invoked command (with user, timestamp, PWD) to /var/log/sudo-commands.log via /etc/sudoers.d/command-logging (Defaults logfile=... + Defaults !syslog), keeping those entries out of /var/log/secure, /var/log/messages, and the journal. Verified with root and a temporary test user, then restarted node1 and confirmed the config, log file, and correct behavior survived a real reboot (boot_id changed).
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (CentOS Stream 10), sudo version 1.9.17p2, and baseline sudoers/logging config
Captured baseline evidence of sudo commands appearing in /var/log/secure and journalctl (authpriv facility) before change
Created /etc/sudoers.d/command-logging with 'Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"' and 'Defaults !syslog', validated with visudo -cf
Installed the sudoers snippet with correct 0440 root:root perms, pre-created /var/log/sudo-commands.log with 0600 root:root perms
Verified new sudo commands (run as root) logged to the new file with user/timestamp/PWD/COMMAND and no longer appear as COMMAND= lines in /var/log/secure, journalctl, or /var/log/messages

Created a temporary test user 'sudologtest' with sudo rights, ran a sudo command as that user, confirmed the log correctly attributed the command to 'sudologtest' and it stayed out of the general system log
Cleaned up the temporary test user and its sudoers entry
Captured baseline boot_id and log/config state, then triggered systemctl reboot on node1 (ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until reachable again and confirmed boot_id changed, proving a real restart occurred
Post-restart, re-verified sudoers config file, log file content persisted, ran a new sudo command to confirm continued correct logging, and confirmed no COMMAND lines in /var/log/secure

evidence.requirement: sudo commands are logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user and timestamp
evidence.summary: After installing the sudoers snippet, subsequent sudo commands (run as root and as test user 'sudologtest') were recorded in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with timestamp, invoking user, PWD, and COMMAND fields.

evidence.requirement: these entries are kept out of the general system log
evidence.summary: Baseline showed sudo COMMAND= lines in /var/log/secure and journalctl before the change; after adding 'Defaults !syslog', tail/grep of /var/log/secure, /var/log/messages, and journalctl -t sudo show no COMMAND= entries for any subsequent sudo invocation (root or sudologtest).

evidence.requirement: sudoers config is syntactically valid and correctly installed
evidence.summary: visudo -cf validated the snippet before install; final file placed at /etc/sudoers.d/command-logging with 0440 root:root permissions.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline captured before restart
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id (cce73776-a7f7-4f32-b822-95d105c52a64) along with sudoers config and current log file contents prior to reboot.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart executed safely with acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Issued 'systemctl reboot' backgrounded so the trigger command returned before the connection dropped; stream closure confirms the reboot proceeded.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Node was unreachable immediately after reboot (connection reset), then came back with boot_id 316d203c-8b2b-4777-97e6-b48341fd9a35, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery: sudo command logging still functions correctly and stays out of general log
evidence.summary: After reboot, sudoers config and log file content were intact; a fresh sudo command was correctly appended to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user/timestamp, and no COMMAND= lines appeared in /var/log/secure, confirming full recovery of the required configuration and behavior.

attempts.summary: Configured sudo on node1 to log every sudo-invoked command (with user, timestamp, PWD) to /var/log/sudo-commands.log via /etc/sudoers.d/command-logging (Defaults logfile=... + Defaults !syslog), keeping those entries out of /var/log/secure, /var/log/messages, and the journal. Verified with root and a temporary test user, then restarted node1 and confirmed the config, log file, and correct behavior survived a real reboot (boot_id changed).
